Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-08
Time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Redwood Solutions Architect), Dr. Alicia Chen (Head of ML, Orion), Marcus Velez (Platform Lead), Samira Noor (Product PM), Ethan Park (Security)
Links shared: Golden prompts spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/golden/ORION_v1.csv), POC SOW draft (link: https://redwood.ai/sow/orion-draft), benchmark workbook (link: https://redwood.ai/bench/orion)

Summary (auto):
- Goal: agree on POC success criteria focused on quality/regression detection and realistic workload sizing.
- Approach: establish a golden prompt set, automated regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring rubric (weighted metrics), baseline benchmarks on Redwood sandbox, then a 3-week POC with staged rollouts.
- Immediate asks: customer to share sampled logs and target SLAs; Redwood to share golden prompt CSV and run initial sandbox benchmark.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick roll call, then we want to run through the POC scope — focusing on quality evals.
[00:00:12] Dr. Alicia Chen: hi — Alicia here. we care a lot about hallucinations in clinical summaries and strict format for downstream ingestion.
[00:00:19] Marcus Velez: Marcus here. also interested in throughput: avg tokens per request, peak concurrent, p95 latency targets.
[00:00:25] Jordan Lee: great. to frame expectations: our typical POC has two parts — quality evaluation (golden prompts, regression tests) and performance/scale benchmarks against your traffic profile.
[00:00:38] Samira Noor: can you define what you mean by golden prompts? how many do you usually need?
[00:00:44] Jordan Lee: sure. golden prompts are a curated set of prompts with expected outputs and grading rules. for Orion we recommend 150-300 prompts covering the common and edge cases: short triage notes, long discharge summaries, templated outputs, and multi-step reasoning items.
[00:01:01] Dr. Alicia Chen: 150-300 sounds reasonable. we can prioritize 50 high-risk examples first — the ones that have caused downstream failures.
[00:01:08] Maya Patel: perfect. we'll take those 50 as the initial golden set and map them to evaluation checks.
[00:01:15] [00:01:20] Jordan Lee: evaluation checks we typically run: format conformance (exact match on JSON schema or regex), hallucination detection (factuality scoring & heuristics), toxicity/safety screens, and a regression delta check vs baseline model. scoring is weighted: 40% factuality, 30% format/structure, 20% relevance/intent, 10% latency.
[00:01:40] Marcus Velez: curious about hallucination detection — how automated is that? do you need human labels?
[00:01:48] Jordan Lee: good Q. we do a hybrid approach: automated heuristics + knowledge-backed checks for named entities, cross-checking against customer-provided canonical data where available. then we sample a stratified subset for human review — typically 10% of failures for triage.
[00:02:05] [00:02:20] Samira Noor: and regression tests? is that like snapshot testing of outputs?
[00:02:27] Liam Ortega: yeah sort of. we run the golden prompts across a baseline model and the candidate model/config. regression is defined as any weighted score drop beyond a threshold — e.g., >5% drop in the aggregate score or more than 2% increase in hallucination rate triggers a fail.
[00:02:43] Dr. Alicia Chen: what about format strictness? some of our downstream jobs rely on exact JSON keys and ordering.
[00:02:50] Jordan Lee: we can do strict JSON schema validation, whitespace-normalized exact matches, and token-level diffs. we report both pass/fail and a fuzzy similarity score (Levenshtein or token overlap).
[00:03:04] [00:03:20] Marcus Velez: workload sizing — our production has a median of 1.8 qps, peak 15 qps across the cluster, avg tokens per request ~420, p95 response size about 1k tokens.
[00:03:34] Maya Patel: good data, thanks. for the sandbox benchmark we'll run: 1) synthetic replay to mimic your token distribution, 2) burst tests to 2x peak (30 qps) to validate autoscale, 3) long-tail stability run 1 hour to surface memory/KV-cache issues.
[00:03:52] [00:04:10] Jordan Lee: we need a sample of logs to create a realistic replay — anonymized. you mentioned 1 week earlier?
[00:04:16] Marcus Velez: yes — we'll export a sampled week's worth, thankfully sanitized.
[00:04:22] Samira Noor: timeline? how long until we get initial quality numbers?
[00:04:27] Maya Patel: typical cadence: day 0-3 collect assets (prompts, logs, schema), day 4-7 Redwood builds golden set and baseline runs, day 8-12 sandbox benchmarks + extended regression runs, day 13-21 iterate on tuning and present final report. so roughly 3 weeks but we can accelerate parts if you prioritize.
[00:04:50] [00:05:05] Dr. Alicia Chen: success criteria — can we write these down now. my prefered thresholds: hallucination rate < 2% on sampled clinical summaries, format conformance >= 98%, overall weighted score >= 90%, latency p95 < 350ms for typical requests.
[00:05:22] Jordan Lee: those are tight but achievable with the right model and quantization profile. note: tradeoffs exist — aggressive quant can reduce cost but may increase hallucination and drop the factuality score. we'll include recommended quant profiles in Optimize outputs.
[00:05:40] Maya Patel: also call out fallback policies: if p95 latency spikes or hallucination breaches threshold, we'll trigger automatic fallback to a more robust model variant or increase dedicated vCPU/GPU routing per policy.
[00:05:55] [00:06:10] Ethan Park: on security side, we need to validate SSO (SAML) for the console, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs retention. can you include SOC 2 docs?
[00:06:20] Liam Ortega: yes — we'll attach SOC2 Type II material, KMS integration guide, and the private VPC pattern docs. note the transcript may show 'K V M S' in auto text, sorry.
[00:06:35] [00:07:00] Samira Noor: scoring approach — you mentioned weights earlier. can we see an example scoring rubric?
[00:07:06] Jordan Lee: example rubric (we'll upload a spreadsheet): each prompt gets per-check scores: factuality (0-100), format (0-100), relevance (0-100), latency penalty in milliseconds normalized to 0-100. aggregate score = 0.4*factuality + 0.3*format + 0.2*relevance + 0.1*(100 - latency_penalty). pass if aggregate >=90 and no critical failures (e.g., hallucination producing a fake med name).
[00:07:32] [00:07:45] Dr. Alicia Chen: how do you detect hallucination in clinical context? name hallucinations are the worst.
[00:07:51] Jordan Lee: we have heuristics: entity cross-checks against provided canonical tables (drug lists, procedure codes), contradiction detection relative to prompt context, and external fact-check step where applicable. anything flagged goes to human review to calculate a true positive rate and tuned threshold.
[00:08:12] [00:08:30] Marcus Velez: any gotchas with private deployment vs hosted? our preference is VPC for compliance but we need predictable throughput.
[00:08:39] Liam Ortega: VPC/Private will give you control and data residency, but we need to size GPU pools accordingly. for the POC we'll run on Redwood Dedicated sandbox nodes in your target region to simulate network/routing.
[00:08:55] Maya Patel: cost note: we can run initial quality evals on smaller instances since load is low, but the scale benchmark will need the same hardware family as production to reflect latency correctly.
[00:09:08] [00:09:25] Samira Noor: regression tests cadence — is it nightly during the POC?
[00:09:31] Jordan Lee: during the POC we'll run nightly regression on the golden set and an hourly smoke regression on a sampled 20 prompts. for production we recommend a CI-triggered regression on model changes.
[00:09:46] [00:10:00] Dr. Alicia Chen: can we also include format-specific checks for CSV and HL7-ish outputs?
[00:10:07] Jordan Lee: yes — we can configure format validators: CSV schema checks, HL7 segment validators, and JSON schema enforcement. failures are categorized as soft (tolerable) or hard (breaking downstream).
[00:10:23] [00:10:40] Marcus Velez: what about adversarial prompts / prompt injection?
[00:10:45] Liam Ortega: we include safety testing with adversarial prompt corpus, check for instruction following boundaries, and hard-blocking patterns. we'll also test function-calling safety if you use tools.
[00:10:59] [00:11:20] Samira Noor: what's the sample size for human review? you said 10% of failures earlier, but what's the min?
[00:11:27] Jordan Lee: min sample is 200 examples or 10% of failures whichever is higher — that gives statistical signal.
[00:11:40] [00:11:55] Maya Patel: I'll summarize the POC plan in the follow-up email: assets needed, golden prompt schedule, benchmarks, scoring rubric, and next meeting.
[00:12:05] Dr. Alicia Chen: sounds good. quick question: will you run temperature/beam vs deterministic configs for comparison?
[00:12:12] Jordan Lee: yes — we test a small matrix: temperature 0.0, 0.3, 0.7; quant profiles (fp16, int8 q8_0, q4_0) and beam/deterministic settings where applicable. we log sample outputs and diff them.
[00:12:28] [00:12:45] Marcus Velez: for the benchmark, can you capture token-level cost breakdowns per route? we want to estimate unit economics in the report.
[00:12:53] Liam Ortega: yes — Redwood Console will show per-route token counts, p95 latency, and cost attribution — we'll include cost projection sheets.
[00:13:08] [00:13:20] Samira Noor: how granular is the hallucination metric? straight count or severity buckets?
[00:13:27] Jordan Lee: severity buckets: minor (small factual mismatch that doesn't change action), moderate (could cause user confusion), critical (could lead to unsafe clinical action). the POC threshold focuses on criticals — target < 0.2% critical, overall hallucinations <2%.
[00:13:47] [00:14:05] Dr. Alicia Chen: do you annotate hallucinations automatically or via services? we may want to own the label set.
[00:14:12] Jordan Lee: you can own labeling; we recommend shared labeling in an agreed schema. Redwood can provide annotation templates and run the first pass to accelerate.
[00:14:25] [00:14:40] Maya Patel: operational playbook: when a regression triggers, we'll do a root-cause: prompt-category analysis, model/config delta, and propose mitigations (prompt engineering, temperature change, fallback). we'll present RCA in the weekly sync.
[00:14:55] [00:15:20] Marcus Velez: any requirement we should be aware of for the replay tool? e.g., timestamp reconstruction, sessions?
[00:15:27] Jordan Lee: replay tool needs prompt text, approximate token counts, user/session id (hashed), and desired response length. timestamps help for simulating diurnal patterns but aren't required.
[00:15:45] [00:16:00] Samira Noor: can we have a canary plan post-POC? small percentage of production traffic to the new model with automatic rollback?
[00:16:08] Liam Ortega: yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts with automatic fallback policies based on health checks and the same evaluation metrics we discussed.
[00:16:22] [00:16:45] Dr. Alicia Chen: security: will the sandbox run in a VPC and encrypt everything at rest?
[00:16:51] Liam Ortega: sandbox for POC can be a dedicated VPC with KMS encryption at rest and in transit. if you need on-prem we have that option but it'll add set-up time.
[00:17:05] [00:17:30] Maya Patel: closing — recapping next steps: Redwood sends golden prompt template + rubric and POC SOW by 2025-05-11; Orion shares anonymized logs and priority 50 examples by 2025-05-14; schedule benchmark week of 2025-05-19.
[00:17:48] Marcus Velez: appreciate that — one more ask: include a lightweight eval dashboard snapshot in the report we can share with execs.
[00:17:56] Jordan Lee: will do — we'll include executive summary charts: hallucination trend, format pass rate, latency distribution, cost projection.
[00:18:12] Samira Noor: thanks, everyone.
[00:18:15] Maya Patel: thanks all — we'll follow up via email and save the artifacts in the shared drive.
[00:18:20] [End of recorded transcript — remainder of time used for screen share and Q&A not fully captured by auto-transcript]

Notes on imperfections: speaker attribution occasionally shifts (auto transcript); a few acronyms parsed incorrectly (KMS shown as K M S), minor punctuation runs-on.

POC artifacts to be produced by Redwood:
- Golden prompt set (CSV) with expected outputs and regex/schema validators.
- Baseline model outputs for regression comparison (archive).
- Benchmark results: latency, throughput, memory/KV cache behavior, autoscale response.
- Eval report: per-prompt scoring, hallucination severity buckets, cost projections, RCA for any failures.

Success Criteria (agreed in call):
- Aggregate weighted score >= 90 across golden set
- Hallucination critical rate < 0.2%, overall hallucination rate < 2%
- Format conformance >= 98% on schema-validated prompts
- Latency p95 < 350ms on production-like hardware during typical load
- Regression delta < 5% in aggregate score vs baseline

Benchmark plan summary:
- Day 1-3: assets, golden prompt priority list (customer provides 50 high-risk examples)
- Day 4-7: Redwood builds golden set, runs baseline, shares initial rubrics
- Day 8-12: sandbox benchmark (replay + burst + 1-hour stability), nightly regressions begin
- Day 13-21: tuning, human review sample labeling, final report and executive summary
